body.heading: Where does the sun go at night?
paragraphs: Every morning, the sun climbs into the sky. Every evening, it sinks away, and the dark comes. It looks as if the sun is travelling around us. But here is the wonderful secret: the sun is not moving across our sky at all. WE are moving.
The Earth — our whole planet, with all its oceans and cities and gardens — is spinning, slowly and steadily, like a top that never stops.

body.heading: Stop and think
paragraphs: Imagine you are sitting on a merry-go-round, turning slowly, and your friend stands still holding a lamp. Would the lamp seem to move around you — even though your friend never walks? Hold that idea, and read on.

body.heading: The great spin
paragraphs: Earth takes one whole day and night — twenty-four hours — to spin around once. When your part of Earth turns to face the sun, sunlight falls on you: that is daytime, and the moment it begins is sunrise.

As Earth keeps turning, your part slowly turns away from the sun. The sun seems to sink — that is sunset — and then your side faces the dark of space: night, with the moon and stars. The sun has not gone anywhere. It is shining on the other side of the world, giving other children their morning.
While you sleep tonight, children across the ocean are eating breakfast in sunshine made by the very same sun.

body.heading: Words to know
paragraphs: Spin — to turn around and around in one place, like a top.
Sunrise — the moment your part of Earth turns into the sunlight.
Sunset — the moment your part of Earth turns away from the sunlight.
Planet — a huge world of rock or gas that travels around a star. Earth is our planet; the sun is our star.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. If Earth stopped spinning for one whole day, what would happen to the side facing the sun — and to the side facing away?
2. When it is night for you, name one thing children on the sunny side of Earth might be doing right now.

takeaway: Day and night come from Earth's spin: as our side turns toward the sun we get sunrise and day; as it turns away we get sunset and night.
